clue.text: Old gun in church in Derbyshire town

indicators.note: in tells us the church abbreviation sits inside the name of the town

parts.note: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: An antique firearm is on display in a church in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early musket fired by a slow-burning match, so it is an old gun.

clue.text: Fellow to crawl out of lake, one that's swamped?

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: out of says the lake abbreviation is removed from the crawling word

parts.note: to grovel is to crawl or abase oneself

explanation.surface: A man hauls himself out of a lake, half-drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops L from GROVEL. 'swamped' suggests overwhelmed; the question mark points to a swamp tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are trees growing in tidal swamps, standing with their roots under water.

clue.text: Language used by almost a million

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A language is spoken by close to a million people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Resentment splitting husband and maybe young male dependants

indicators.note: splitting says the resentment word breaks apart the pair that follows

parts.note: a son is an example of a young male
anger is resentment or wrath

explanation.surface: Bitterness drives a wedge between a father and his son, both relying on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the son as only one example of a young male, so the definition-by-example is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are people who attach themselves to others for gain, living as dependants.

clue.text: Animal work leads to very big money

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work; leads to just says it comes first
OS stands for outsize, very big
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: An animal's labours bring in a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Ship crossing strait followed by river bird

indicators.note: crossing says the ship goes over, enclosing what follows

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, a coal barge

indicators.note: followed by puts the river letter after the strait abbreviation

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for strait

explanation.surface: A vessel passes through a narrow channel, with a river and a bird beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel here is not the hull's spine but an old word for a flat-bottomed coal barge on the Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon known for hovering, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Young child missing final drama in cartoon film

indicators.note: missing final says the drama word is dropped from the end of the child word

parts.note: bambino is Italian, borrowed into English, for a baby or small child
No (or Noh) is the classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A toddler is denied the last bit of a play at a cartoon screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing final' drops NO from the end of BAMBINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the 1942 Disney animated feature about a young deer.

clue.text: Brought up without love and disaffected

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reared word goes round the love letter

parts.note: bred means brought up or raised
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone raised in a loveless home grows up alienated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here means outside, so BRED goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bored means weary and uninterested, close to disaffected or disengaged.

clue.text: Men in deal — I'm out to get right purchasing system

indicators.note: in says the soldiers go inside the scrambled letters
out signals that the letters of deal and I'm are put out of order

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are men in the army as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A gambler counts himself out of a hand to get men's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the letters to MAILDE, which the parse does not spell; OR, other ranks, is army usage for enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is a way of buying goods by post from a catalogue, a purchasing system.

clue.text: Bars offering foul stingo

indicators.note: foul means fouled up or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pubs serve a nasty strong ale.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO is an old word for strong beer, which makes 'Bars' look like pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are bars of cast metal such as gold.

clue.text: At end of declaration sign name in classical style

indicators.note: At end of picks out only the closing letter of the word declaration

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: Someone signs their name with a flourish at the bottom of a formal statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb telling you to sign your name; it is the noun, a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomen is the Latin word for name, specifically a Roman's clan name, so it is a name in classical style.

clue.text: Watching amount eaten by Russian runner

parts.note: the Ob is a great river of Siberia; a runner is crossword code for a river
a serving is an amount of food dished out

explanation.surface: Someone watches a Russian athlete wolfing down a helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but rivers run: here it is the Ob.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing is a synonym of watching, both meaning keeping one's eyes on something.

clue.text: Inside the car the Queen waves

indicators.note: Inside places the royal abbreviation within the name of the car

parts.note: a Rolls (Rolls-Royce) is the archetypal luxury car
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch waves to the crowd from inside her limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' reads as the Queen's gesture, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollers are long heavy waves breaking on a shore, so the word is a synonym for waves.

clue.text: King's man attached to company, facing army in revolution?

indicators.note: facing means the first piece stands in front of the rest, face to face

parts.note: the Red Army was the army of the Russian revolution, so RED
at can mean attached to, as in a doctor at a hospital

explanation.surface: A royal soldier joins a firm while confronting a rebel army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' looks like a reversal signal, but the question mark points to the Red Army of 1917. The answer also recalls the British soldiers of the American Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A redcoat was a British soldier, serving the Crown, so a king's man.

clue.text: I've delirium and it's somehow producing an apparent reality

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified new order

explanation.surface: A feverish patient boasts that their ravings feel convincingly real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' shuffles the letters of I'VE DELIRIUM IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Verisimilitude is the quality of seeming true or real, an appearance of reality.

clue.text: Man who's wicked and deranged turning up in port

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a man who behaves badly

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: mad means deranged

explanation.surface: A villainous madman arrives at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses MAD to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a Dutch city and one of the busiest seaports in Europe.

clue.text: Supports in bays perhaps to hold shelf up

indicators.note: to hold means the tree word goes round the other piece

parts.note: bays are laurel trees, so bays are an example of trees

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the shelf word is read upwards

parts.note: a sill is a shelf below a window

explanation.surface: Brackets in alcoves are needed to keep a shelf in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bays' suggests alcoves; they are laurels. 'up' turns SILL to LLIS, held by TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Number in favour of corporal punishment given a hearing

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: given a hearing says the punishment word is what is heard spoken

parts.note: the cane was the stick used for corporal punishment in schools

explanation.surface: Many people back the return of school beatings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure; it is something that numbs, a local anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Procaine is a local anaesthetic, a drug that numbs, so a number.

clue.text: Such is eNORMously outstanding leader!

parts.note: the word eNORMously carries a norm, another word for a standard, inside it, so it bears a standard; and an outstanding leader is one who carries the flag at the front

explanation.surface: An exceptional leader is praised in gushing terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mark NORM, a synonym of standard, held inside the word enormously: the word is literally a bearer of a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carries the flag in battle, and figuratively is a leading figure of a cause.

clue.text: The drink? More than one sailor in this is lost

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, so ABS are sailors
taken as written

indicators.note: is lost says the letters of is are taken out of this

explanation.surface: Sailors ask about the drink that got them lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lost' removes IS from THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Uncongenial accommodation gets muck over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: dung is muck or manure
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Grim lodgings turn filthy as the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell, hardly pleasant lodgings.

clue.text: Shoot something for Christmas dinner?

definitions.meaning: a shoot is a new growth from a plant
the Brussels variety is a traditional British vegetable served at Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a young shoot, and Brussels sprouts are the classic British Christmas vegetable.

clue.text: Small place with comforts and delights

parts.note: PL is the short form of place, as in street addresses
eases means comforts or soothes

explanation.surface: A cosy little spot with home comforts is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to delight, so pleases and delights are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Only one not left with superficial injury

indicators.note: not says the left abbreviation is missing from the word for only one

parts.note: single means only one

explanation.surface: Only one person came away with a minor wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops L from SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight burn to the surface, a superficial injury.

clue.text: Provincial group in charge of African people

parts.note: Northern Ireland is called the Province, abbreviated NI
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: A regional committee runs affairs for an African community.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'the Province' means Northern Ireland, giving NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic describes the peoples of the Nile valley region, such as the Dinka and Maasai.

clue.text: Country knight wearing classical attire

indicators.note: wearing means the knight is inside the garment

parts.note: the toga was the garment of ancient Rome
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A nation's knight turns up in Roman robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts N inside TOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom in the South Pacific, so a country.

clue.text: Canon has gold ball stuck outside home

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: stuck outside says the dance word is wrapped around the home word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
in means at home

explanation.surface: A cathedral clergyman owns a golden ball lodged outside his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a cathedral clergyman, but it is a rule or law.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or decree, and an ordinance is an authoritative order, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Law handed down here: offence attracts fine

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
A1 means first-rate or fine, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A court where justice is dispensed finds that wrongdoing brings a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' suggests a penalty, but it means excellent: A1, read as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where Moses received the Ten Commandments, so the law was handed down there.

clue.text: Valley with moderate climate lacking merit

indicators.note: lacking says the merit word is taken away from the climate word

parts.note: temperate describes a mild, moderate climate
to rate is to merit or deserve

explanation.surface: A mild-weathered valley is described as having nothing special about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes RATE from TEMPERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a celebrated valley in Thessaly, Greece, famous in classical poetry.

clue.text: Workers given fish as introductory offer?

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Staff receive fish as a promotional deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introductory offer' sounds like a sales gimmick; the question mark flags the hand offered when introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: When people are introduced they offer a hand to shake, so the greeting is an offer made at an introduction.
